title: Workshop
repoLine: {repo} · {count, plural, one {# worktree} other {# worktrees}} on this Mac

sessions.status: Atlas reads {tool}'s own session list to show which sessions wait for you. While Workshop is open it runs {command} every 10 seconds, and a second after a {tool} session starts or ends, with no network access. Atlas writes nothing.
sessions.off: Atlas does not run {tool}, so no room can say whether its session waits for you or has finished replying.
sessions.unreadable: Atlas could not read {tool}'s session list: {reason}
sessions.fallback: Until it can, no room can say whether its session waits for you. Atlas tries again within 10 seconds.

reason.notFound: {tool} was not found in the folders Atlas looks in.
reason.unknownForm: The list was in a form Atlas does not know; a newer {tool} may have changed it.

reads.title: What this screen reads
reads.promise: Read on this Mac only; nothing is saved or sent.

list.label: Session status
list.caption: Shows which session waits for your answer.

names.label: Session names
names.caption: Shows the name each session has.

pulse.label: File changes
pulse.caption: Lights the room and counts changes as files change.

load.label: Memory, CPU, GPU
load.caption: Shows use per room and for this whole Mac.

names.status: A room shows the name {tool} gives each session, so you can match it to the terminal or window it runs in. A name can be a title {tool} wrote from your conversation. Atlas keeps the last names it read in memory until you switch names or the session list off, or quit the app; it never writes them to a file or a log, sends them anywhere, or gives them to an agent.
names.off: Atlas does not read session names. Rooms call a session by its tool and number, such as {example}.
names.needsList: Session names come from the session list, which is off.

sessionLine.more: {count, plural, one {and # more session} other {and # more sessions}}

room.quietMinutes: {count, plural, one {Quiet for # minute} other {Quiet for # minutes}}
room.quietHours: {count, plural, one {Quiet for # hour} other {Quiet for # hours}}
room.quietDays: {count, plural, one {Quiet for # day} other {Quiet for # days}}
room.untouched: {count, plural, one {Untouched for # day} other {Untouched for # days}}
room.notInBase: {count, plural, one {# commit not in {branch}} other {# commits not in {branch}}}

monitor.unreadableLock: The lock names no session Atlas can read
monitor.lastHourChanges: {count, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} in the last hour
monitor.areasMore: {count, plural, one {and # more folder} other {and # more folders}}

pulse.status: While Workshop is open, macOS tells Atlas each time a file changes in one of this repository's worktrees, and Atlas counts the changes. It does not open the files and keeps no file name. Changes inside .git and to files Git ignores are not counted. Counts stay in memory for an hour.
pulse.off: Atlas does not watch for file changes. A room shows a change the next time Atlas reads Git, up to a minute and a half later.
pulse.lastMinute: {count, plural, one {# file change} other {# file changes}} in the last minute
pulse.lastHour: {count, plural, one {# file change} other {# file changes}} in the last hour
pulse.onlyOpen: Atlas counts only while Workshop is open.
pulse.none: No file change was counted here in the last hour.
pulse.noAgent: Files are changing here, and Atlas sees no agent in this folder.
pulse.unwatched: macOS could not watch this folder, so this room shows a change only when Atlas reads Git.

load.status: Every 5 seconds while Workshop is open, Atlas reads how much memory and CPU each agent and the commands it started are using, the memory and CPU of a Java program outside them, such as a Gradle daemon, and how busy this Mac's memory, CPU and GPU are. It reads each program's name, never its command line. Nothing is written and nothing leaves this Mac.
load.off: Atlas does not read memory, CPU or GPU use, so no room or heading shows them.
load.moreGroups: {count, plural, one {and # more kind} other {and # more kinds}}
load.agentElsewhere: {who} itself is counted in {branch}, the folder it was started in. This room counts only the commands it runs here.
load.none: No agent program is running in this room, so there is no load to show.
load.mac: This Mac: memory {used} of {total} · CPU {cores} of {coreCount} cores · GPU {gpu}%
load.macNoGpu: This Mac: memory {used} of {total} · CPU {cores} of {coreCount} cores
load.gpuWhy: macOS reports GPU use for the whole Mac. Naming the program that uses it needs administrator rights, which Atlas does not ask for.
load.gpuMissing: This Mac did not report GPU use.
load.failed: Atlas could not read load from macOS just now and tries again in 5 seconds. Everything else in this room is unaffected.

shelf.mergedList: {count, plural, one {# worktree merged into {branch}} other {# worktrees merged into {branch}}}
shelf.untouchedList: {count, plural, one {# worktree untouched for 7+ days} other {# worktrees untouched for 7+ days}}

unreadable: {repo} could not be read. Choose the repository folder again to grant access.

choose.title: Choose the Git repository your agents work in

empty.title: Only {branch} for now
empty.body: Each new worktree opens a room here. When Claude Code or Codex starts working, you see it.

quiet.title: Nothing in {repo} is at work
quiet.body: Merged and long-untouched worktrees wait on the shelf below.

web.title: Workshop runs in the desktop app
web.body: A browser cannot run git or read this computer's processes. In this browser you can still open your folder's map and Library.

notRepository: {folder} is not a Git repository. Choose the folder that holds your project's .git.

header.pointToLoad: Show the rooms using the most

git.uncommitted: {count, plural, one {# file changed, not committed} other {# files changed, not committed}}

now.waiting: {who} has stopped and is waiting for you. Answer it in the terminal or app where that session runs.
now.sessionFailed: {who} ended with an error. Its work so far is still in this folder.
now.replied: {who} has finished its reply and is waiting for your next message.
now.working: {who} is working in this folder now.
now.twoTools: {who} are working in this one folder at the same time, so their changes can collide.
now.resting: {who} holds this folder but has not changed anything for a few minutes.
now.dozing: {who} holds this folder, but nothing has changed for more than {minutes} minutes.
now.merged: Everything here is already in {branch}. The folder can be removed.
now.locked: The folder is locked, but Atlas cannot tell which session locked it.
now.lockLeft: The session that locked this folder has ended, and its lock is still here.
now.missing: Git still lists this worktree, but its folder is gone.
now.unheld: No session is working in this folder.

panel.filesMore: {count, plural, one {and # more file} other {and # more files}}
panel.cleanupTitle: To clear it, run this in a terminal
panel.quiet: No commits since {branch} and no uncommitted files.

about.label: What this screen shows
about.body: One room is one worktree: a separate folder of this repository where a branch is being worked on. Each screen shows the branch, its newest commits and the files changed but not committed yet. A room is lit while an agent session is working in it. Press a room to see the rest.

landed.title: Merged into {branch}
landed.note: One line is one merged pull request; a commit pushed without one is a line too. Atlas reads this Mac's copy of the branch, so a change you have not pulled yet is not listed.
landed.none: Nothing has been merged into {branch} yet.
landed.squashed: It was merged as one commit, so there are no separate commits to show.
landed.unreadable: Atlas could not read this change's commits and files from Git. Close it and open it again to retry.
